title: Presenting Numbers That People Remember
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：数据汇报

sections.heading: 1. A Number Alone Means Nothing
paragraphs: Here is a sentence from a real quarterly review.
"We reduced P ninety-nine latency from eight hundred and forty milliseconds to six hundred and ten."
It is accurate, it is impressive, and almost nobody in the room will remember it by lunch.
The problem is not the audience's attention span.
A number by itself has no ==meaning== until people can compare it to something.
Is six hundred and ten good?
Is the drop big or small?
Most listeners have no ==reference point==, so the number simply __slides past__ them.
**Your job is not to report numbers; it is to make them feel like something.**
That takes three small habits, and none of them require ==fancy== charts.
paragraphs_zh: 这是一次真实的季度复盘里的一句话。
「我们把 P99 延迟从八百四十毫秒降到了六百一十毫秒。」
数据准确，成绩亮眼，但到午饭时间，屋里几乎没人还记得。
问题不在于听众注意力不集中。
一个数字本身没有意义，除非大家能拿它跟什么东西比一比。
六百一十算好吗？
这个降幅算大还是算小？
大多数听众没有参照物，所以这个数字就这么从他们耳边滑过去了。
你的工作不是汇报数字，而是让数字有感觉。
这需要三个小习惯，而且都用不着花哨的图表。

sections.heading: 2. Round It, Compare It, Translate It
paragraphs: First, round ==aggressively==.
"About a third faster" is easier to hold in your head than the exact figure.
Put the precise number on the slide for those who want it, and say the simple one out loud.
Second, always give a comparison.
A comparison gives listeners a ruler to measure your number against.
Compare it to last quarter, to a ==competitor==, or to a goal everyone remembers.
"We're now faster than our target for next year" __tells a story__ in one line.
Third, translate the number into human units.
Instead of "saved twelve thousand compute hours," try "saved the cost of two full-time engineers."
Instead of "point three percent error rate," try "one failed payment for every three hundred customers."
**People forget percentages, but they remember people, money, and time.**
Finally, choose one ==headline== number per slide, and __let the rest go__.
If everything is highlighted, nothing is.
A clear number respects how people actually listen, which is once, quickly, and while thinking about something else.
paragraphs_zh: 第一，大胆取整。
「快了大概三分之一」比精确数字好记得多。
精确数字放在幻灯片上给想看的人看，嘴上说简单的那个。
第二，永远给一个对比。
对比给了听众一把尺子，用来衡量你的数字。
跟上季度比，跟竞争对手比，或者跟一个大家都记得的目标比。
「我们现在已经比明年的目标还快了」，一句话就讲了个故事。
第三，把数字换算成人能感知的单位。
别说「省了一万两千个计算小时」，试试说「省下了两个全职工程师的成本」。
别说「错误率百分之零点三」，试试说「每三百个客户里有一笔支付失败」。
百分比人们会忘，但人、钱和时间他们记得住。
最后，每页幻灯片只选一个核心数字，其余的都舍掉。
如果什么都高亮，就等于什么都没高亮。
一个清晰的数字，尊重的是人们真实的听法：只听一遍，听得很快，而且脑子里还想着别的事。

gist.q: 为什么作者说单独一个数字没有意义？
gist.a: 听众没有参照点，不知道这个数字是好是坏、变化是大是小，所以记不住。

gist.q: 让数字被记住的三个习惯是什么？
gist.a: 大胆取整；一定给出对比（上季度、竞品、目标）；换算成人、钱、时间等直观单位。

gist.q: 每页幻灯片的数字应该怎么安排？
gist.a: 只选一个主打数字，其余放下；全都强调等于什么都没强调。

prompts.q: 季度汇报中，你要讲“崩溃率从百分之零点八降到百分之零点二”。用 30 秒把这个数字讲得让人记住：取整、对比、换算成人话。
prompts.ref: The headline for this quarter is stability. Our crash rate is now about a quarter of what it was in the spring. To put that in human terms, before, roughly one in every hundred and twenty sessions ended in a crash. Now it's one in five hundred. For a typical user who opens the app twice a day, that's going from a crash every two months to about one a year.
prompts.ref_zh: 这个季度的关键词是稳定性。我们的崩溃率现在大约只有春天时的四分之一。换成人能感知的说法，以前大概每一百二十次会话就有一次崩溃。现在是五百次一次。对一个每天打开两次 app 的普通用户来说，就是从大概两个月崩一次，变成了一年崩一次左右。

prompts.q: 你要向管理层争取资源优化存储，说明“每月存储费用十五万美元，其中三成是无用日志”。用 30 秒把钱换算成大家有感觉的单位。
prompts.ref: Here's the number I want you to remember. About a third of our storage bill is old logs that nobody ever reads. That's roughly fifty thousand dollars a month, or the cost of a small team, spent on data we delete without looking. With about three weeks of cleanup work, we can get most of that back, every single month, from now on.
prompts.ref_zh: 这是我希望大家记住的数字。我们存储账单里大约三分之一，是从来没人看的旧日志。这差不多是每个月五万美元，相当于一个小团队的成本，花在了我们看都不看就删掉的数据上。只要花大概三周做清理，从今往后每个月都能把其中大部分省回来。

words.ex: This metric has no meaning unless we compare it week over week.
Last year's peak gives us a useful reference point for capacity.
We don't need a fancy dashboard; a simple table is enough.
We're cutting scope aggressively to hit the date.
Our sign-up flow is two steps shorter than any competitor's.
The headline number is a forty percent drop in tickets.
Keep demos short; everyone's attention span drops after lunch.
Let's round it to two seconds on the slide.
The cost savings from the migration were impressive.
